QCOM.thesis_one_line: The chip-maker behind most premium Android phones is shifting to cars and data centres, but phone sales are falling and the price already assumes the shift works.
key_adverse_facts: Q3 FY26 handset revenue fell 20% to $5,086M and non-GAAP EPS fell 20% to $2.21; Apple is expected to use its own modems increasingly (10-Q 0000804328-26-000086).
Cash conversion weakened: 9M FY26 free cash flow $6,827M vs $9,231M, Q3 FCF $495M, inventory $8,379M vs $6,526M at 28 Sep 2025.

25,000,000-share Amazon warrant at $161.26 issued 3 Sep 2026 (8-K 0001104659-26-105718) plus 17,826,566 shares issued for Modular; stock up 37% from 31 Jul low to $201.97, above the $194 mean analyst target; CEO sold 10,000 shares each on 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-25.
data_conflicts: Triage (Q12) cited 17% forward EPS growth; d4 consensus shows FY27 EPS 10.18 vs FY26 10.48, i.e. -3%.
Yahoo FCF 10.24B matches OCF minus capex of 10.4B TTM, but ignores 3.24B TTM share-based compensation that non-GAAP EPS also excludes.
Q2 FY26 GAAP EPS 6.88 and Q4 FY25 GAAP EPS -2.89 are driven by a 5.7B deferred-tax valuation allowance charge and release; b1/d4 trailing GAAP figures are distorted.
QCOM.confidence_in_thesis: medium: near-term guidance has been met or beaten five of five quarters and the balance sheet is sound, but the growth case (non-handset $40B by FY29) is unproven and the price already discounts it; earnings date is Yahoo-sourced, not company-confirmed

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for QCOM. Reverse DCF implies about 14.5% a year free-cash-flow growth after stock pay (7.8% before) at a 9.5% cost of equity, versus about 5% in my base case (non-handset revenue about 24B by FY29, handsets falling, FY29 non-GAAP EPS about 12).

QCOM.scenario_basis: Start price 201.97, FY26 non-GAAP EPS about 10.5 (guide-implied) and TTM FCF 10.4B (7.2B after SBC); bear FY29 EPS 8.5 at 13x, base 12.0 at 17x, bull 15.5 at 20x; dividends 11.0/11.6/12.0 over 3 years from 3.68 a share (1.9%).
kill_criteria: Non-GAAP diluted EPS below $2.05 for Q4 FY26 or below $1.80 in any later quarter.
QCT handset revenue falls below $4.5B in any quarter of FY27, or China handset revenue has not returned to sequential growth by Q1 FY27 as guided.
TTM free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures, consolidated) below $8.0B at any quarter-end.
Consolidated debt (short- plus long-term, carrying value) above $20B, or inventory above $9.5B while revenue is below $10B a quarter.
No disclosed data-centre revenue (reported as its own line) by the FY27 Q2 report (May 2027), or the Amazon warrant vesting above 12,500,000 shares without matching disclosed revenue.

NTRS.thesis_one_line: A custody bank that safeguards about $20 trillion for institutions and rich families; a good business with strong capital, but the share price already reflects it.
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 EPS of $4.23 includes a $525.4M pre-tax Visa exchange-offer gain; ex-notable EPS is about $2.97 and TTM ex-notable about $10.67 versus Yahoo trailing $11.64 (release 0000073124-26-000043).
Recurring 'one-off' charges: severance $85.2M in 2024, $58.8M in 2025 and $51.0M in Q2 2026, plus $61.5M software disposals in Q2 2026.

CFO David Fox plans to retire around 31 Mar 2027 (8-K 0000073124-26-000057, filed 2026-09-29, after the information cutoff); consensus FY27 EPS 12.59 is below FY26 12.73 and the mean target is only 4.9% above the price.
data_conflicts: Yahoo FY26 consensus EPS 12.73 and trailing EPS 11.64 include the Visa gain; ex-notable run-rate is about 11.7 for FY26.
d4 shows no FCF yield and Yahoo operating cash flow of only $0.53B TTM; cash-flow measures are not meaningful for a bank.
Triage said forward EPS growth 8.9%; d4 NTM EPS 12.63 vs FY26 ex-notable 11.7 is about 8% but FY27 consensus is below FY26 GAAP-inclusive.
NTRS.confidence_in_thesis: medium: capital, credit quality and fee momentum are verified in the 10-Q, but valuation leaves no margin of safety and earnings are market-sensitive; the earnings date is Yahoo-sourced and no numeric company guidance exists

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for NTRS. At 9.5% cost of equity and 85% payout the price implies about 3.4% a year aggregate net-income growth from ex-notable FY26E (5.1% from TTM), versus about 3.4% in my base (2% for three years then 4%). P/B of 2.57x needs a sustainable ROE near 18% versus about 16.5% ex-notable TTM.

NTRS.scenario_basis: Start price 175.73, ex-notable FY26E EPS 11.7 (Q1 2.71, Q2 2.97, H2 about 6.0); bear FY29 EPS 9.8 at 11.5x, base 14.0 at 15x, bull 17.0 at 16.5x; dividends 10.0/11.0/11.5 over 3 years from 3.52 a share annualised (2.0%).
kill_criteria: Northern Trust Corporation CET1 ratio (standardized, consolidated) below 10.5% at any quarter-end, or a stress capital buffer above 3.5%.
Trust, Investment and Other Servicing Fees down more than 5% year on year in any quarter.
Non-interest expense excluding notable items up more than 6% year on year for two consecutive quarters, or pre-tax margin (FTE) excluding notables below 28%.
Return on average common equity excluding notables below 13% for two consecutive quarters.
Nonaccrual loans above 0.6% of total loans, or a quarterly provision for credit losses above $75M.

HAL.thesis_one_line: An oil-field services company that drills and completes wells worldwide, priced as if profits never recover while its finances are strong and overseas contracts are growing.
key_adverse_facts: Adjusted EPS fell from $2.99 (2024) to $2.42 (2025) and TTM is $2.37; Q2 2026 adjusted operating margin 12.0% vs 13.2% a year earlier and Completion and Production margin down 140bp (release 0000045012-26-000057).

Middle East/Asia revenue fell 10.7% YoY to $1,298M on the regional conflict; North America revenue rose only 0.8% YoY despite 'recovery' commentary; a Mexican customer is about 7% of receivables with payment delays.
Insiders sold about $25.6M in Form 4 filings since March 2026 with no purchases, including CEO sales at $40.00 (2026-03-30) and $35.00 (2026-08-19); price is 24% below the 52-week high.
data_conflicts: Triage called momentum strong (+52%); the stock is 24% off its 52-week high and down from $37.29 on 3 Sep to $32.76.
Yahoo FCF 2.05B TTM vs my OCF minus capex 1.73B vs company-defined 1.94B (adds asset-sale proceeds).
d4 flag: epsCurrentYear 2.35 vs quarterly trend differs by more than 10%; adjusted EPS 2026 H1 is 1.10 versus consensus FY26 2.35.
HAL.confidence_in_thesis: low-to-medium: valuation and balance sheet are verified from filings, but the earnings recovery rests on one quarter of North America improvement and management commentary, there is no numeric guidance, and insiders are net sellers; the earnings date is Yahoo-sourced

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for HAL. Reverse DCF implies about 3.9% a year free-cash-flow growth (1.8% on company-defined FCF) at 9.5% cost of equity, versus about 6-8% in my base case (FY29 adjusted EPS about 3.0, FCF about 2.3B).

HAL.scenario_basis: Start price 32.76, TTM adjusted EPS 2.37 and FCF 1.73B (OCF minus capex); bear FY29 EPS 2.04 at 9.5x, base 3.00 at 13x, bull 4.00 at 15x; dividends 2.04/2.04/2.10 over 3 years from 0.68 a share (2.1%).
kill_criteria: Adjusted operating margin (non-GAAP, consolidated) below 11.0% for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026: 12.0%).
Consolidated net debt (total debt carrying value minus cash) above $7.0B, or net debt/TTM adjusted EBITDA above 2.0x (now about 1.2x).
TTM free cash flow (operating cash flow minus capital expenditures, consolidated) below $1.2B at any quarter-end (now $1.73B).
North America revenue below $2.1B in any quarter through Q2 2027 (Q2 2026: $2.28B), or total quarterly revenue below $5.3B.
Full-year 2026 shareholder returns (dividends plus buybacks) below 50% of free cash flow, the company's stated framework, or a quarterly dividend cut below $0.17.
